correctness.rationale: For b_j=P^j(1), the weight-zero identity inductively gives b₁b_j=(j+1)b_(j+1), so P(1)^p=p!b_p=0. If a≠0 has valuation r, its p-th power is zero exactly when pr≥N (its leading coefficient remains nonzero over any field). For sufficiency the t^i a^j with 0≤i<r and i+rj<N are a triangular basis with unit leading coefficients. The group for each i is invariant under a, since the last basis vector maps to zero by truncation; hence the projection π onto i=0 is k[a]-linear. The target subalgebra has length L=ceil(N/r)≤p. Truncated integration a^j↦a^(j+1)/(j+1), zero at the top, uses only 1 through L−1. On a pair a^i,a^j the two sides have common degree i+j+2 and vanish if that degree is truncated, including if an input is top degree. Otherwise the integration denominators are units and the usual reciprocal identity applies. The subalgebra-linearity of π pulls the identity for integration back to the whole algebra, giving P(1)=a. This argument works over the coordinate ring k[a_r,a_r^(-1),a_(r+1),…,a_(N−1)] itself: the triangular diagonal is invertible there and exactly the same basis, projection and multiplication identities apply. This proves the section as a morphism, not just by agreement at field points. The zero section and the finite-field count follow. An independent enumeration of all linear maps in the five listed prime-field/truncation configurations reproduced valid-operator counts 2, 4, 24, 3, 15 and distinct unit-value counts 2, 2, 4, 3, 9, with the exact predicted sets.
residual_risks: No scheme-theoretic image or global section is implied by the reduced stratum sections.
The frozen construction checks in nonprime finite fields were inspected, not independently rerun; universality over arbitrary fields follows from the algebraic proof, not finite checks.

originality.rationale: The divided-power obstruction, the square-zero case, and additional low-depth/rank-one sectors are covered and are not counted as new. The inspected results do not imply the arbitrary-depth converse for elements with a^p=0 but a²≠0, nor the general regular valuation-stratum sections. For example, p=3, N=6, a=t² is on the claimed locus but a²=t⁴≠0; a rank-one operator with this unit value cannot satisfy a²=2P(a), since its image would be ka and a² is not proportional to a. No dominating arbitrary-depth, all-positive-characteristic locus theorem was found in the bounded comparison.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently formulated general algebraic extension theorems are not ruled out by these bounded checks.
No global priority determination is made; small-depth and rank-one overlaps are expressly credited.

Guo–Yu universal obstruction and indexed low-depth/rank-one comparisons
value.rationale: Evaluation at the unit is a natural invariant of a unital Rota–Baxter algebra. The universal necessary obstruction alone leaves it unclear whether a prescribed generator can be realized on the fixed ambient algebra. Solving that realization problem for all depths and giving regular families of witnesses makes the result useful for constructions and moduli comparisons. The predictable finite-field count is a consequence, not the sole value.
residual_risks: Does not classify all operators or determine the global scheme image, and does not enumerate all finite-field operators.
